A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same COUNTDOWN research. All 17 pages of each version, including Appendices A-D, are readable, and the equations, algorithms, figures and tables can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original downstream-task, AlpacaEval, kernel-latency and throughput experiments on four LLMs, plus sparsity-signal and predictor analyses in Section 6.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and their results in the main text and appendices, including Tables 1-4, 7, 11 and 12.

M1.justification: Sections 3-4 and Algorithms 1-3 retain the same sparsity criteria, threshold calibration, low-rank predictor training and inference kernels. Revised headings and notation explanations do not change the procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions use ARC-Easy/Challenge, HellaSwag, PIQA, WinoGrande, OpenBookQA, TruthfulQA and GSM8K, together with AlpacaEval 2.0 conversational evaluation. No training domain, evaluation task or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: The reported tables and figures retain the same comparator membership, including CATS, Deja Vu and Dense where applicable. v2 newly names CHESS in Section 5, but supplies no corresponding result, figure entry or identifiable evaluated comparison; this mention does not establish an added baseline.

E3.justification: The four evaluated LLMs, sparsity settings, dataset subsets and test sizes, ideal/practical evaluation distinction, and throughput generation lengths remain unchanged. Appendix B.1 newly discloses training duration rather than revising a previously stated training budget.

E4.justification: The CIF/CAF comparison of sparsity indicators in Figure 4 and the TernaryLinear versus low-rank predictor analysis in Table 4 are retained unchanged. No ablation, robustness test or supplementary analysis is added.

E5.justification: Table 5 retains seed 42 and explicitly states that experiments used a single run without multiple random seeds. Neither version adds confidence intervals, significance tests or another uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: Appendix B.1 newly reports predictor training times of 2 or 4 hours, predictor sizes of 576-900 MB, and a stated 6-7% parameter overhead. These are additional resource figures; the existing benchmark scores, throughput measurements, predictor-quality results and plotted findings are unchanged.

T1.justification: The derivations, shared-index property, CIF/CAF definitions and Appendix D cost formulas are retained. Adding the missing component index [i] after the product following Equation 5 clarifies the already-defined relation s = u ⊙ h rather than changing the mathematical argument.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the weighted-sum sparsity framework, complementary M-COUNTDOWN and D-COUNTDOWN contributions, and the same headline performance and acceleration claims.

C2.justification: Interpretations of predictor limitations, M-COUNTDOWN's signal advantage and TernaryLinear's runtime tradeoff remain unchanged. Both versions retain the limitations concerning single-batch greedy decoding and magnitude-based sparsity criteria.

D1.justification: v2 adds practical resource information in Appendix B.1: predictor training takes 2 hours for Llama/Gemma and 4 hours for Phi/Qwen on one A100, with reported sizes of 576-900 MB. Hyperparameters, software versions, hardware specifications and pseudocode otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 5 adds a limited reference to CHESS as a comparator, rendered as 'CHESS ()' without a completed citation or bibliography entry. The related-work discussion, existing bibliography and broader novelty positioning are unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 standardizes FFNN to FFN, makes small grammatical corrections, explains Equation 6's subscripts, renames several headings and adds acknowledgments. The overall narrative and section organization remain intact.

P2.justification: The same five figures and twelve tables are retained. Figure 1's caption terminology changes, and text reflow shifts displays such as Table 2 and Algorithm 1; there is no substantive redesign or new visual analysis.

improvement.justification: The new training-time and predictor-size disclosure in Appendix B.1 modestly improves assessment of practical resource requirements, while notation and terminology edits improve clarity. Scientific methods and experimental support remain unchanged. The unsupported 'CHESS ()' comparison claim introduces a small reporting defect, but the resource disclosure provides a limited net improvement.
